blocks.content: Syllogism consists of two or more statements (premises) followed by conclusions. You must decide which conclusions follow logically.  CGL asks 3–4 syllogism questions per paper, making it extremely important.

cells: TYPES OF STATEMENTS IN SYLLOGISM

Universal Positive (A): ALL A are B → Full circle of A inside B

Universal Negative (E): NO A is B → Circles of A and B completely separate

Particular Positive (I): SOME A are B → Circles partially overlapping

Particular Negative (O): SOME A are NOT B → Part of A outside B

blocks.content: Draw Venn diagrams for the given statements and check if each conclusion diagram is ALWAYS true (definite conclusion) or SOMETIMES true (possible conclusion).

cells: Statement Pair
Valid Conclusions
All A are B + All B are C
All A are C (definite)
All A are B + No B is C
No A is C (definite)
Some A are B + All B are C
Some A are C (definite)
Some A are B + No B is C
Some A are not C (definite)
All A are B + Some B are C
Some C are A (possible, not definite)
No A is B + All C are B
No A is C (definite)
Some A are B + Some B are C
No definite conclusion about A and C
All A are B + All C are B
Some A may or may not be C (no definite)

blocks.content: Ex.1 Statements: All dogs are animals. All animals are living things. Conclusions: I. All dogs are living things. II. All living things are dogs.
Sol. Dogs ⊂ Animals ⊂ Living things. Conclusion I: All dogs are living things ✓ (definite). Conclusion II: All living things are dogs ✗ (reverse not true). Ans: Only I follows
Ex.2 Statements: No cat is dog. Some dogs are lions. Conclusions: I. Some lions are not cats. II. No lion is cat.

Sol. No cat=dog, some dogs=lions. The 'some dogs' that are lions → those dogs are not cats (since no cat is dog). So some lions are not cats. But ALL lions could be non-cats? Not necessarily since some dogs are lions and those dogs aren't cats. Conclusion I: Some lions are not cats ✓. Conclusion II: No lion is cat — not definite (some lions not shown to be dogs might be cats). Ans: Only I follows
Ex.3 Statements: All roses are flowers. Some flowers are red. Conclusions: I. Some roses are red. II. Some red things are flowers.

Sol. Roses ⊂ Flowers. Some Flowers = Red. The red flowers may or may not be roses. Conclusion I: Some roses are red — NOT definite (possible but not certain). Conclusion II: Some red things are flowers ✓ (since some flowers are red, those flowers are red → some red = flowers). Ans: Only II follows
Ex.4 Statements: Some books are pens. No pen is a pencil. Conclusions: I. Some books are pencils. II. Some books are not pencils.

Sol. Some books = pens. No pen = pencil. So the books that are pens → not pencils (since pens ≠ pencils). So SOME books are not pencils (the ones that are pens). Conclusion I: Some books are pencils — NOT certain (books might not overlap with pencils). Conclusion II: Some books are not pencils ✓. Ans: Only II follows
When neither conclusion I nor II alone follows, but together they cover all possibilities (complementary pair), the answer is 'Either I or II follows'.

cells: NOTE: For Either-Or: One conclusion must be Universal Positive and the other Particular Negative of the SAME subject and predicate. Example: 'All A are B' and 'Some A are not B' form a complementary pair.

blocks.content: From  2016 onwards, questions use phrases like 'Some A being C is a possibility' or 'All A being B is a possibility'. The rule: a possibility is TRUE unless it is DEFINITELY FALSE.

cells: POSSIBILITY RULES

If 'No A is B' is definite → 'Some A are B' is NOT a possibility.

If 'All A are B' is definite → 'Some A are not B' is NOT a possibility.

If 'Some A are B' is definite → 'No A is B' is NOT a possibility.

In all other cases, the possibility is VALID (true).

blocks.content: Q.39 All mangoes are fruits. All fruits are tasty. Conclusions: I. All mangoes are tasty. II. Some tasty things are fruits.
Ans: (c) Both I and II Hint: All mangoes are fruits (⊂tasty) → All mangoes tasty ✓. Fruits ⊂ tasty → some tasty = fruits ✓.
Q.40 No table is chair. Some chairs are wooden. Conclusions: I. No table is wooden. II. Some wooden things are not tables.

Ans: (b) Only II Hint: From 'some chairs are wooden' and 'no table is chair' → those wooden chairs are not tables → some wooden are not tables ✓. But other wooden things might be tables → I not definite.
Q.41 All A are B. No B is C. Conclusions: I. No A is C. II. All C are A.
Ans: (a) Only I Hint: A⊂B, B∩C=∅ → A∩C=∅ → No A is C ✓. II is not supported.
Q.42 Some doctors are engineers. All engineers are lawyers. Conclusions: I. Some doctors are lawyers. II. All lawyers are engineers.
Ans: (a) Only I Hint: Some doctors=engineers, engineers⊂lawyers → those doctors are lawyers → some doctors are lawyers ✓. II reverses the universal → not valid.
